newsitem.title: USA: Qualcomm says court rules against it.
newsitem.headline: Qualcomm says court rules against it.

text.p: Qualcomm Inc on Friday said a federal judge has issued a temporary restraining order through April 23 affecting the company's newly developed "Q" phone, a wireless telephone.
"This restraining order does not involve any of Qualcomm's CDMA technology patents," Qualcomm said in a statement.

The ruling stems from a patent infringement case brought against Qualcomm by Motorola Inc in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California. Motorola claims Qualcomm is infringing on certain design patents it holds.

"We are confident that the court, once it has benefit of facts not available to it when this temporary restraining order was granted, will agree our 'Q' phone does not infringe on anyone's design patents," Qualcomm said.
It said it would continue shipping its other products.
CDMA is the company's code division multiple access technology for delivering digital voice and data communications over wireless networks.
